summary: We developed TerraPulse, a free, bilingual (EN/ES), mobile-first web platform for urban families, farmers and companies or municipalities in the windy Patagonian steppe. Users pick an illustrated soil card instead of entering lab data, and TerraPulse produces a full agronomic plan plus a custom-sized biodigester with an interactive, dimensioned blueprint, from the inlet pump to the crop roots. To address Field Shift, it combines live NASA POWER API data (wind, frost, rain, radiation, soil wetness) with NISAR 200 m soil moisture, SMAP Freeze/Thaw and ECOSTRESS layers (simulated in this prototype) to tell users how, with what and when to sow, fertilize and harvest. The fertilizer comes from a closed digester that sanitizes every batch at 70 °C for 60 minutes. This matters because it keeps sewage and fish waste out of urban lagoons and coasts in Santa Cruz, such as Laguna de los Patos, ends odors whatever the wind direction, replaces up to 89 % of fertilizer costs (modeled in USD and ARS), and works as a ground analog for pressurized NASA Artemis ISRU greenhouses on Mars.
details:
What it does & How it works

TerraPulse is a free, bilingual (EN/ES) web platform that turns NASA Earthdata into a step-by-step plan for farming and circular waste management in the windy, arid Patagonian steppe of Santa Cruz, Argentina. It works in three stages:

  1. Universal configurator. Users choose their scale: urban household or community garden (10–500 m²), farm or ranch (1–10,000 ha), or company/municipality (tonnes of waste per day). They enter their area, people or livestock, location and target crops. Instead of asking for lab parameters, TerraPulse shows four illustrated soil cards (arid & windy, saline with white crust, oil-stained TPH soil, fertile black soil), each with a surface view and a 0–30 cm cross-section. The user taps the one that looks like their land, and the app loads the hidden technical parameters behind it.
  2. NASA-powered agronomic engine. The app pulls live daily data from the NASA POWER API (wind speed and gusts, minimum temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, surface soil wetness). It combines these with NISAR (200 m soil moisture), SMAP Freeze/Thaw and ECOSTRESS (evaporative stress) layers; in this prototype those three layers are simulated with realistic values. From this it computes the exact N-P-K requirement, seed and water needs, and a growing-degree-day (GDD) calendar. The output is a plain-language plan: HOW to plant (mandatory no-till direct seeding against wind erosion), WITH WHAT (biofertilizer dose in m³/ha) and WHEN (sowing, fertilizing and harvest dates). An animated 0–50 cm root profile shows soil recovery from year 0 to year 5, and every result has a “Why does this calculation matter?” explanation.
    • P-101 inlet grinder pump;
    • insulated R-101 reactor at 37.2 °C;
    • gas train and G-101 CHP engine with heat recovery;
    • mandatory sanitary pasteurizer at 70.4 °C for 60 min, with interlock valve XV-104;
    • P-104 fertigation pump, with valve FCV-105 adjusted by soil moisture;
    • drip irrigation into the crops and roots.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Cleaner water and coasts. Sewage, fish waste and manure go to a closed digester instead of urban lagoons and the sea. This targets the eutrophication of Laguna de los Patos (Pico Truncado) and the Caleta Olivia coastline; our model estimates a 78 % reduction in lagoon pollution load.
  • No odors, whatever the wind direction. Waste is treated in a sealed reactor, not in open ponds, so the wind no longer carries the smell into neighborhoods.
  • Less imported fertilizer. In our 50 ha ranch example, sanitized biofertilizer replaces about 89 % of the fertilizer cost (≈ USD 8,700/year) and covers 100 % of the crop’s nitrogen.
  • Own energy and lower emissions. The example ranch produces about 141 kWh/day of net electricity and recovers 9.8 kWth of heat, with a design EROI of 3.4×. It avoids about 66 tCO₂eq/year (methane GWP₁₀₀ = 28).
  • Soil and water recovery. Organic matter rises from 0.9 % to 2.0 % in 5 years, water retention increases by about 29 % (field studies report +20 % to +35 %), and roots go from 8 to 33 cm deep.
  • 10-year financial shield (2026–2036, USD & ARS). Four economic frames are modeled: base, energy subsidy removal (+45 %), fertilizer crisis (+60 %) and carbon credits. Payback ranges from 41 to 70 months depending on scale and frame, while inaction accumulates growing losses. Industrial plants can also sell surplus biofertilizer by the tonne.
  • From Patagonia to Mars. The same closed-loop architecture (waste → bioreactor → sanitation → soil) is a ground analog for NASA Artemis ISRU greenhouses. There, heat from a surface fission reactor would wash perchlorates out of regolith (design target < 0.01 %).

Tools, Programming Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Languages and front end: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Tailwind CSS (CDN), Google Fonts.
  • Graphics: interactive, animated SVG drawn in code, including the blueprint with ISA-5.1 tags, viewBox zoom, soil profiles, financial charts and illustrated soil cards. There are no external maps or images.
  • Data access: a fetch call to the NASA POWER Daily API with a timeout, plus an embedded 2001–2025 climatology fallback for offline use.
  • Agronomic and engineering models: Hargreaves ET₀, growing degree days, N-P-K balance, digester mass and energy balance, thermal losses at −10 °C, and NPV/IRR/payback calculations.
  • NASA data: NASA POWER (live). NISAR, SMAP Freeze/Thaw and ECOSTRESS (simulated in the prototype, ready for real data). Landsat/MODIS as references.
  • Hardware: runs in any browser on phones and PCs; responsive, mobile-first design.
  • AI assistance: Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini for code prototyping, UI/UX structuring and bilingual translation. All scientific, agronomic and engineering models were reviewed and validated by our team.

Why it is Creative

  • Cognitive translation. A farmer, a family or a municipal officer does not need to know their soil’s pH or organic matter. They only pick the illustration that looks like their land, and satellite data turns into “how, with what and when” instructions anyone can follow.
  • Universal design. One tool serves an urban family, a sheep rancher and a municipality. It is usable by people aged 10 to 60+, in English and Spanish, on phones and computers.
  • A living blueprint. Instead of a static diagram, the full plant from the inlet pump to the plant roots is an interactive engineering drawing, computed for each user, with zoom into 6 stations and data sheets for every piece of equipment.
  • A Patagonia–Mars bridge. Wind, cold, salinity and degraded soils make the Patagonian steppe a real-world testbed for closed-loop life support on Mars.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Extreme Patagonian climate. Gusts above 60 km/h make no-till seeding and wind-aware irrigation mandatory. Winters down to −10 °C require sizing the reactor insulation and recovering heat from the CHP engine to keep stable mesophilic digestion at 37.2 °C. During months when SMAP shows frozen soil, the digestate is stored in tank TK-103 for up to 120 days.
  • Biosafety. Every batch must stay 60 minutes at 70.4 °C; valve XV-104 does not release the batch until the cycle is complete. Digestate from urban sewage is restricted to forage, windbreak forestry and bioremediation of oil-contaminated (TPH) soils, never to vegetables eaten raw.
  • Intermittent connectivity. If the NASA POWER API does not respond within 5 seconds, the app switches to an embedded climatology and keeps working offline.
  • Honesty and human validation. Simulated layers and design values are labeled as such. TerraPulse assists and never replaces the agronomist: every plan should be checked with soil analysis, a germination test, the 70 °C certificate and sign-off from INTA and local agronomists.
